subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Listening and Speaking: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
overview: In this sub-strand you will learn to say the sounds /t/, /d/, /f/ and /v/ and the sound pair /tw/ clearly, using words about the family. You will practise minimal pairs and tongue twisters, use family words such as sibling, relative and care-giver in your own sentences, and listen carefully to a short family story and answer questions about it.

lessons.title: The sounds /t/ and /d/ and the sound pair /tw/
objectives: Say the sounds /t/ and /d/ clearly and hear the difference between them.
Say words that begin with /tw/, such as twin and twelve.
Explain why saying sounds correctly helps the listener.
lessons.intro: Say the words ten and den aloud. Only one sound is different, yet the meaning changes completely. If you mix up the two sounds, your listener may not understand what you mean.
lessons.notes:
### How to make /t/ and /d/
Put the tip of your tongue on the hard ridge just behind your top teeth. Stop the air for a moment, then let it go with a small puff.

- For /t/, your voice box is quiet. Put your fingers on your throat and say /t/: you feel nothing.
- For /d/, your voice box buzzes. Say /d/ with your fingers on your throat and you feel a buzz.

So the tongue does the same work for both sounds. The only difference is the voice.

### Minimal pairs
A minimal pair is two words that differ in only one sound. They help us hear and practise the difference.

- ten – den
- tie – die
- town – down
- tear – dear
- bat – bad
- cart – card

Notice that the sound can be at the beginning (ten, den) or at the end (bat, bad) of the word.

### The sound pair /tw/
In words like twin, twelve, twenty, twice and between, the sound /t/ is joined straight to /w/. Round your lips for the /w/ while you are still saying /t/. Do not put a small vowel between them. Say twin, not tu-win.

Family words with these sounds: twin, daughter, dad, aunt, adopt, duties, elder, relative, visitor.

### Why pronunciation matters
When you say sounds correctly, people understand you the first time. Your grandmother, your teacher and a visitor from another county will all get your message. Everybody's accent is a little different, and that is fine. What matters is that the important sounds are clear, and that we listen to one another with respect.

keyWords.meaning: the smallest piece of speech that we hear, such as /t/ or /d/
two words that are the same except for one sound, such as ten and den
one of two children born to the same mother at the same time
a sentence with many similar sounds that is hard to say quickly

examples.problem: Which word has the /d/ sound at the end: bat or bad?
steps: Say both words slowly.
Listen to the last sound. bat ends with /t/, bad ends with /d/.

examples.problem: Say this tongue twister three times, slowly and then faster: Twelve twins took ten tidy towels to Dad.
steps: Tap the table each time you hear /t/ or /tw/.
Keep the /tw/ in twelve and twins together, with no vowel in between.
examples.answer: The /tw/ words are twelve and twins; the /t/ words are took, ten, tidy and towels; the /d/ words are tidy and Dad.

activity.title: Minimal pair cards
materials: Small cards or pieces of paper
steps: In pairs, write each word of these minimal pairs on its own card: ten/den, tie/die, town/down, bat/bad, twin/win.
Mix the cards and put them face down.
One learner picks a card and says the word without showing it.
The partner points to the word they heard among the cards on the table. Check together if it is correct.
Swap roles. Then say the tongue twister: Twelve twins took ten tidy towels to Dad.

practice.question: Write the minimal pair partner of town that begins with /d/.
Is your voice box quiet or buzzing when you say /d/?
Write three words that begin with the sound pair /tw/.
practice.answer: Any three, for example twin, twelve, twenty, twice, twig.

practice.question: Why is it important to pronounce ten and den correctly?
practice.answer: They are different words with different meanings, so a wrong sound can give the listener the wrong message.

summary: /t/ and /d/ are made in the same place; /d/ uses the voice and /t/ does not.
Minimal pairs such as ten and den help us hear one-sound differences.
In /tw/ words, join /t/ and /w/ with no vowel between them.

lessons.title: The sounds /f/ and /v/ and family vocabulary
objectives: Know the meaning of family words such as relative, sibling, care-giver, orphan and elder.
Use family words correctly in spoken sentences.
lessons.intro: When visitors come to your home, you may introduce them to your family: This is my father, my sister and my aunt. To do this well you need the right family words and clear sounds.
lessons.notes:
### How to make /f/ and /v/
Gently touch your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow air out between them.

- /f/ has no voice. Your throat is quiet: fan, family, father, friend, laugh (here the letters gh make /f/).
- /v/ has voice. Your throat buzzes: van, visitor, love, have, very.

Minimal pairs: fan – van, fine – vine, few – view, safe – save, leaf – leave, ferry – very.

Take care: many speakers say /b/ instead of /v/, as in bery for very. Keep your teeth on your lip for /v/; do not close both lips.

### Family words
- family: a group of people related to each other, such as parents and their children
- relative: a person in your family, like an aunt, uncle or cousin
- sibling: a brother or sister
- care-giver: a person who looks after a child, for example a grandmother or guardian
- orphan: a child whose parents have died
- widow: a woman whose husband has died
- clan: a large group of families who share the same ancestors
- ancestor: a person in your family who lived long ago, before your grandparents
- elder: an older, respected person in a family or community
- mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in-law: relatives a person gets through marriage. When a man marries, his wife's mother becomes his mother-in-law and his wife's brother becomes his brother-in-law.
- adopt: to take a child into your family legally and bring him or her up as your own
- chore: a small job done regularly at home, such as sweeping or fetching water

### Using the words in sentences
A good sentence shows that you know what the word means:

- My elder brother helps me with my homework.
- Our family has five members: my parents, my two siblings and me.
- Mrs Wanjiru adopted a baby girl and loves her very much.
- Every Saturday I do my chores before I visit my friends.

keyWords.meaning: a member of your family, such as an uncle, aunt or cousin
a person who looks after a child
a small regular job at home

examples.problem: Complete the sentence with the correct word: My mother's sister is my ____.
steps: A mother's sister is a female relative from the mother's side.

examples.problem: Use the word visitor in a sentence and underline the /v/ sounds.
steps: visitor begins with /v/.
Add another /v/ word to practise, such as very.
examples.answer: We had a very kind visitor on Sunday. (/v/ in very and visitor)

activity.title: Family word game
materials: A dictionary or a digital device, if available
steps: In groups, sort the cards into two piles: words with /f/ (family, father, friend, father-in-law) and words with /v/ (love, visitors, relative, have).
Check the pronunciation of any hard word in a print or electronic dictionary.
Each member picks two cards and says a sentence that uses both words.
The group claps once if the sentence is correct and the /f/ or /v/ sound is clear.
With your teacher's help, search the internet for two more family words and use them in sentences.

practice.question: Write the /v/ partner of each word: fan, few, safe.
What do we call a brother or sister?
Use the word elder in a sentence.
practice.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: The elders of our village settle disagreements peacefully.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: A child whose parents have died is called an ____.

summary: /f/ and /v/ are made with the top teeth on the bottom lip; /v/ uses the voice.
Family words include sibling, relative, care-giver, elder, ancestor and clan.
A good sentence shows the meaning of the new word.

lessons.title: Listening comprehension: A visit to Grandmother
objectives: Listen attentively to an oral text about a family.
Answer questions about what you heard.
Notice how clear pronunciation helps listening.
lessons.intro: A good listener looks at the speaker, keeps still and thinks about what is being said. Today your teacher or a partner will read a short story aloud. Listen carefully, because you will answer questions without looking at the text.
lessons.notes:
### How to listen well
- Look at the speaker and keep quiet.
- Listen for who is in the story, where it happens and what happens.
- Picture the events in your mind.
- If you miss something, wait until the end and then ask politely for it to be repeated.

### The listening text (to be read aloud by the teacher or a partner)

Twins in the Family

Akinyi and Atieno are twins. They are ten years old and they live with their father, their mother and their little brother, Otieno. During the December holiday, the family travelled to visit their grandmother in the village.

Grandmother was waiting at the gate. She hugged the twins and said, "You have grown so tall! I cannot tell who is who." Everyone laughed.

In the evening, Grandmother told them about their ancestors and about their clan. She said that in the old days, the elders met under a big fig tree to talk about the needs of the village. The twins listened quietly.

The next morning, everyone shared the chores. Father fetched firewood, Mother cooked, and the twins fed the chickens and swept the compound. Otieno was too young to work, so he played with a little calf.

Before they left, Grandmother gave each twin a small basket. "Remember," she said, "a family that works together stays together."

### Answering questions
Some answers are said directly in the story. For example: Who are the twins? Akinyi and Atieno. Other answers need you to think. For example: Why did Grandmother say she could not tell who was who? Because twins often look alike.

The speaker said twins and ten clearly. If she had said wins or den, you would have heard a different story. Clear speech makes listening easy.

keyWords.meaning: the open area around a home
a family member who lived long ago

examples.problem: Where did the family go during the December holiday?
steps: Listen for the place in the first paragraph.
examples.answer: To visit their grandmother in the village.

examples.problem: Why did Otieno not do any chores?
steps: The story says he was too young to work.
examples.answer: He was too young, so he played with a calf instead.

activity.title: Listen and answer
materials: The story Twins in the Family, read by the teacher or played from an audio recording
steps: Close your books. Listen to the story read aloud once without writing.
Listen a second time and write down the names of the people in the story.
In pairs, answer the teacher's questions orally, taking turns.
Say three words from the story that have /t/, /d/, /f/, /v/ or /tw/ sounds.
Tell your partner one chore you do at home, using a full sentence.

practice.question: What did Grandmother tell the children about in the evening?
practice.answer: About their ancestors and their clan, and how the elders used to meet under a fig tree.

practice.question: Name two chores the twins did.
practice.answer: They fed the chickens and swept the compound.

practice.question: What do you think Grandmother meant by 'a family that works together stays together'?
practice.answer: When family members help one another, they become close and united.

summary: Listen with your eyes on the speaker and your mind on the message.
Some answers are stated directly; others need you to think about the story.
Clear pronunciation by the speaker makes a text easy to understand.

quiz.question: Which pair of words is a minimal pair?
quiz.explanation: ten and den differ in only one sound, /t/ and /d/.

quiz.question: Which word begins with the sound pair /tw/?
Which word begins with the /v/ sound?
quiz.explanation: visitor begins with /v/; the others begin with /f/.

quiz.question: Write the word that changes when /f/ in fan becomes /v/.
quiz.explanation: fan and van are a minimal pair.

quiz.question: A brother or sister is called a ____.
quiz.explanation: Sibling means a brother or a sister.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses the word chore correctly?
options: My chore is my best friend.
Sweeping the house is my daily chore.
The chore visited us on Sunday.
quiz.explanation: A chore is a regular job at home, like sweeping.

quiz.question: Use the word care-giver in a sentence.
quiz.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: My grandmother is my care-giver while my parents are at work.
quiz.explanation: A care-giver is a person who looks after a child.

quiz.question: In the story Twins in the Family, who was waiting at the gate?
quiz.explanation: The story says Grandmother was waiting at the gate.

quiz.question: In the story, what did Grandmother give each twin?
quiz.explanation: Before they left, Grandmother gave each twin a small basket.

quiz.question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?
quiz.answer: So that listeners understand the right message; one wrong sound can change a word, as in ten and den.
